PlayerRecord:
        description: >
            A derived, materialized snapshot of one Player's aggregate
            statistics for one season (year), recomputed as of a given GameDay
            by the updatePlayerRecords action — NOT something a user edits
            directly. `year = 0` conventionally means "all-time" (see
            lib/tables.ts getYearName).
        identity: "unique (playerId, year, gameDayId)"
        keyAttributes:
            stalwart: "Percentage of the SEASON's games that this player played in — attendance/commitment metric, not skill."
            speedy: "This player's average response interval for the season, in the same units as Outcome.responseInterval; lower ranks better. Only shown once responses >= config.minRepliesForSpeedyTable, otherwise the player appears in the 'Unqualified' variant."
            averages: "Mean match points per game for the season; qualification gated by config.minGamesForAveragesTable."
            pub: "Sum of Outcome.pub across the season."
            rank*: "Precomputed rank within that season/table, one column per rankable table — see enumerations.TableName and lib/tables.ts."
        relationships:
            - { predicate: recordOf, range: Player, cardinality: "1" }
            - {
                  predicate: asOf,
                  range: GameDay,
                  cardinality: "1",
                  description: "Which game day this snapshot was computed after.",
              }

            scorePub: "Sum of Outcome.pub across the season."
            rank*: "Precomputed rank within that season/table, one column per rankable table (rankPoints/rankAverages/rankStalwart/rankSpeedy/rankPub, paired with the score* attribute of the same suffix) — see enumerations.TableName and lib/tables.ts."

Everything is green. Here's the final summary.

## Summary

Implemented the plan you approved: renamed `PlayerRecord`'s five cumulative table-ranking fields with a `score` prefix (`scorePoints`, `scoreAverages`, `scoreStalwart`, `scoreSpeedy`, `scorePub`, pairing with the existing `rank*` prefix), freeing up `points` for a new single-game derived field, and rewired `Player.getLastResult` to query it directly instead of building an awkward OR-disjunction against `Outcome`+`GameDay`.

**Schema/migration:** amended the still-uncommitted SYS-581 migration in place (no new migration file) — five `CHANGE COLUMN` renames plus a new `points` column backfilled via the same win/draw/loss rule as `getPlayerPoints`. Applied non-destructively to the local dev DB; applied via `db push --accept-data-loss` to the disposable Playwright DB (you approved both).

**Code:** `PlayerRecord.ts` (derivation + ranking logic), `Player.ts` (`getLastResult` rewrite, now a single indexed lookup), new `PlayerLastResultType` (narrowed return type — confirmed every consumer only reads `.gameDay`), `PlayerInfo.tsx`/`PlayerProfile.tsx`/`TableScore.tsx` plus their specs/stories/mocks.

**Two real bugs caught along the way, not just renames:**
1. `TableScore.tsx` and `PlayerRecord.getTable` both did `playerRecord[table]` — indexing by the `TableName` route enum (`'points'|'averages'|...`) directly as a field name. That silently breaks the moment the enum value and the field name diverge, which is exactly what this rename did for 4 of 5 tables. Fixed by making the mapping explicit (`scoreFieldMap` in `lib/tables.ts`, mirroring the existing `rankMap`) — this would have caused every non-points leaderboard table to throw in production.
2. A production build crash (`ReferenceError: Cannot access ... before initialization`) traced to re-exporting the new type from the `@/types` barrel — it pulled `PlayerLastResultType` into the same module graph as everything else importing `@/types`, tripping a circular-import chain through the generated Prisma Zod schema barrel. Fixed by importing it directly everywhere instead, with a comment explaining why it's the one type file in that directory not re-exported from the barrel.

**Verification:** typecheck/lint/knip/format all clean; services, lib, actions, components, pages, api, storybook suites all passing with 100% coverage maintained on every changed file; full production build clean; full Playwright suite green (the handful of intermittent failures during parallel runs all confirmed as pre-existing resource-contention flakes by passing cleanly in isolation, unrelated to this change). Nothing committed.

# Bring test coverage (mocks, unit tests, Storybook, Playwright) up to date with uncommitted changes

`` is optional. If provided, treat it as a hint restricting scope (e.g. a file path, directory, or feature name). If omitted, operate on the full uncommitted diff.

## Steps

1. **Gather the diff.** Run `git status` and `git diff HEAD` (staged + unstaged) to list every changed file. If `` was given, filter to files matching that hint but still read the full diff for context. If the working tree is clean, tell the user there is nothing to sync and stop.

2. **Classify each changed file by layer**, per `CLAUDE.md`:
   - `src/app/**/page.tsx` / `layout.tsx` etc. → **page** — tests under `test:pages` (`vitest.pages.config.ts`)
   - `src/app/api/**` route handlers → **API route** — tests under `test:api` (`vitest.api.config.ts`)
   - `src/actions/**` → **server action** — tests under `test:actions` (`vitest.actions.config.ts`)
   - `src/lib/core/**` → **action core** — check which config covers it (may be `test:actions` or `test:lib`; confirm via `include` globs in the vitest config files)
   - `src/services/**` → **service** — tests under `test:services` (`vitest.services.config.ts`)
   - `src/lib/**` (excluding `core/`) → **library util** — tests under `test:lib` (`vitest.lib.config.ts`)
   - `src/components/**`, `src/hooks/**`, `src/docs/**` → **component** — tests under `test:components` (`vitest.components.config.ts`); also check for a co-located `*.stories.tsx`
   - `src/types/**` → usually no dedicated test; skip unless it changes runtime Zod validation behaviour (then trace to whichever service/action consumes it)
   - Anything touching a page, form flow, or user-visible behaviour reachable from `e2e/*.spec.ts` → also candidate for **Playwright** coverage

   If a changed file's layer is ambiguous, grep the `include` arrays in `vitest.*.config.ts` to confirm which config actually picks it up rather than guessing.

3. **For each changed source file**, locate its co-located artifacts and decide what's needed:
   - Unit test: `<name>.vitest.spec.ts(x)` next to the file (never in `__tests__/`)
   - Mock: sibling `__mocks__/` directory, matching the pattern already used by neighbouring modules (e.g. `src/services/<Model>/__mocks__/`, `src/lib/__mocks__/`)
   - Storybook: sibling `<name>.stories.tsx` for components — update play-test interactions if props/behaviour changed, add a story if the component is new
   - Playwright: only touch `e2e/*.spec.ts` if the change affects a user-facing flow already covered there, or introduces a new page/flow that has no E2E coverage yet and clearly warrants it

   Decide per file:
   - New file with no test/mock/story → create them
   - Modified file with existing test/mock/story → update to match new behaviour (new branches, new props, new error paths, changed Zod schema, etc.)
   - Modified file whose tests already exercise the changed behaviour → leave as is, but still verify via coverage in step 5

4. **Follow repo testing conventions** while writing/updating tests (from `CLAUDE.md`):
   - Accessible selectors (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, `getByText`) over `data-testid`
   - Don't rely on Mantine internals (generated class names, internal DOM structure)
   - Use the generic query overload (`getByRole<HTMLInputElement>(…)`) instead of `as HTMLInputElement`
   - Don't test generated Zod schemas directly — test service/action behaviour and validation instead
   - E2E specs must be fully parallel-safe
   - Services: validate inputs with Zod before Prisma calls; mock at the Prisma/service boundary, not internals
   - British English in any new comments or copy

5. **Run the relevant test commands with coverage** for every layer touched, e.g.:

   ```bash
   npm run test:services:coverage
   npm run test:components:coverage
   npm run test:api:coverage
   npm run test:actions:coverage
   npm run test:lib:coverage
   npm run test:pages:coverage
   npm run test:storybook
   ```

   Only run the ones matching layers actually touched (running all is fine too if the diff spans many layers).

6. **Check coverage on the changed files specifically**, not just the overall summary. Read the per-file coverage lines in the terminal or `coverage/` HTML/JSON output for each file changed in step 1. If any changed file is below 100% line/branch coverage:
   - Identify the exact uncovered lines/branches
   - Add or extend test cases to cover them (new error paths, edge cases, conditional branches)
   - Re-run the coverage command
   - Repeat until every changed file shows 100% coverage

7. **Run Playwright** (`npx playwright test`) if any E2E-relevant flow was touched or added in step 3. Fix failures by adjusting the spec or, if the app itself has a genuine bug surfaced by the test, flag it to the user rather than silently loosening the assertion.

8. **Run the finalisation checklist** (per `CLAUDE.md` / the `finalise` skill): `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npx knip`. Fix everything — `npm run lint:fix` first for lint, remove unused exports/files/deps for knip. If unsure whether an issue pre-dates this change, `git stash`, re-run to get a baseline, `git stash pop`, and fix only new issues.

9. **Repeat steps 5–8** until: every relevant test command passes, every changed file has 100% coverage, Playwright (where applicable) passes, and typecheck/lint/knip are all clean.

## Done criterion

All test suites relevant to the changed layers pass, every changed source file has 100% unit test coverage (line and branch), Playwright passes for any touched user-facing flow, and `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` / `npx knip` all exit 0 with no warnings. Report a summary: files changed, tests/mocks/stories added or updated per file, final coverage figures for changed files, and confirmation the finalisation checklist is clean.

## Notes

- Never commit changes — leave that to the user.
- Don't chase 100% coverage on generated files (`prisma/generated/`, `prisma/zod/`) or files explicitly excluded in a `vitest.*.config.ts` `coverage.exclude` list (e.g. `*Skeleton*`, `DebugBreakpoints`, `DebugSizeOverlay`, `DebugFontSizes`) — those are intentionally out of scope.
- If a changed file spans multiple test configs' `include` globs (rare), run all configs that could match rather than guessing which one is authoritative.
- If achieving 100% coverage on a changed file requires testing genuinely unreachable code (e.g. a defensive branch guaranteed unreachable by types), say so explicitly and ask the user whether to simplify the code instead of contorting a test to hit it.
- Overall repo policy is ≥90% coverage; this skill's own bar for files it touches is 100% — don't stop early at the lower project-wide threshold.

## Summary

You were right, and my empirical check turned up a nuance worth being precise about.

**Fixed:** all 8 filter predicates in `src/services/PlayerRecord/PlayerRecord.ts` that narrowed `Partial<PlayerRecordType>`/`OutcomeType` fields with `p !== null` — changed to `p != null` (7 in `calculateYearPlayerRecords`'s ranking arrays: `pointsArray`, `averagesArray`, `averagesArrayUnqualified`, `stalwartArray`, `speedyArray`, `speedyArrayUnqualified`, `pubArray`; 1 in `calculatePlayerRecord`'s `responseIntervals`). Confirmed via the generated schema that these fields really are typed `.nullish()` (`number | null | undefined`), not just `.nullable()`, so `undefined` was a genuine runtime possibility the old check let through.

**One thing worth flagging honestly:** I wrote a regression test to prove the corruption, and it forced me to check the actual mechanism empirically. `Array.prototype.sort()` is specified (ECMA-262) to always move `undefined` elements to the end of the array *without ever invoking the comparator on them* — so for this specific code (filter → sort → `indexOf` on already-null-guarded values), the leaked `undefined` doesn't actually scramble the real values' relative order or produce a wrong rank for a scored player. The fix is still unambiguously correct — it removes a type lie (the `is number` predicate was false), and it stops relying on an obscure sort() quirk that would silently break the moment this code did anything else with these arrays (a `.reduce()`, a manual comparison, a different sort implementation). I just want to be accurate about what was and wasn't observably broken rather than overstate it.

**New test:** `upsertForGameDay with an unplayed player mixed in` — mixes a player with real scores against one whose score fields are genuinely left `undefined` (never played, no response interval), and asserts the scored player's ranks are exactly correct (not `NaN`) and the unscored player's ranks stay `undefined` (not `null` — they never enter the ranking `if` guards at all). Verified this test fails against the old `!==` code and passes against the fix.

**Verified:** typecheck, lint, format:check clean; services suite 469/469 passing; 100% coverage maintained on `PlayerRecord.ts`.

**Left alone, flagged only:** two pre-existing occurrences of the same `!== null` pattern in `src/lib/core/submitPicker/submitPicker.ts:277` and `src/services/Player/Player.ts:702` — neither touched by this session's diff, so out of scope unless you want them addressed too.

content.text: This one turns out to be a false positive — let me check `Player.ts:702` too before making any changes.

I looked closely at both, and neither actually has the bug — worth flagging before I touch anything.

**`submitPicker.ts:277`** — `PickerCandidate.age` is a hand-written interface field typed `number | null` (not Prisma's generated `.nullish()`), and I traced every construction site: `age` is always built as `born !== null && born < 1995 ? gameDay.year - born : null` (submitPicker.ts:503-504). It can never be `undefined`.

**`Player.ts:702`** — `effectiveParent` is `Map<number, number | null>`, and the while loop that populates it (line 690-693) self-corrects: even if `parentId` starts as `undefined` (from `p.introducedBy`), the loop condition `parentId !== null` is true for `undefined` too, so it always enters the loop body at least once, and `introducedByMap.get(parentId) ?? null` coalesces any `undefined` lookup result to `null` before `effectiveParent.set()` is ever called. `undefined` can't survive to reach the filter.

So unlike `PlayerRecord.ts` (where the fields were genuinely typed `.nullish()` — `number | null | undefined` — straight from the Prisma-generated schema), these two are provably `number | null` only. Changing `!==` to `!=` here would be behaviorally a no-op and, per the project's "don't add handling for scenarios that can't happen" convention, not something I'd normally do unprompted.

Given that — want me to make the change anyway for stylistic consistency (harmless either way), or leave these two alone since there's no actual defect?

Everything's clean.

## Summary

One correction worth flagging: the non-null assertion itself doesn't throw — `!` is erased at compile time, and `getPlayerPoints`'s `switch` falls through to `default: return null` for an unrecognised status. So the actual pre-fix behaviour was *silent wrong data* (a missing GameDay quietly produced `null` points), not a crash — arguably worse for a leaderboard than a loud failure, which is why I went with the controlled-throw option.

**Fixed** (`src/services/PlayerRecord/PlayerRecord.ts`): `pointsOf` now checks the map lookup explicitly and throws `InternalError` with `gameDayId`/`playerId` context when a `GameDay` is missing — matching the `InternalError` "should not occur" convention already used elsewhere in this codebase (`submitPicker.ts`).

**This immediately caught a real, pre-existing bug**: a test fixture in `PlayerRecord.vitest.spec.ts` computed `gameDayId: index / 10 + 1` without `Math.floor()`, producing fractional IDs (`1.1`, `2.3`, etc.) that never matched the integer-keyed status map — previously silently swallowed as `null` points, now surfaced loudly by the new throw. Fixed with `Math.floor(index / 10) + 1`.

**Added**: a new test (`upsertForGameDay with an outcome referencing an unknown GameDay`) proving the throw fires when an outcome's `gameDayId` isn't in the status map.

**Verified**: typecheck, lint, format:check, knip all clean; full services suite passing with 100% coverage maintained on `PlayerRecord.ts`.

-- Add the new status column as nullable so it can be backfilled before the
-- NOT NULL constraint is enforced.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` ADD COLUMN `status` ENUM('NoGame', 'Scheduled', 'AWin', 'Draw', 'BWin') NULL;

-- Backfill GameDay.status from the columns it replaces:
-- - `game` = FALSE always meant "not an actual match" (covers both a
--   not-yet-scheduled slot and a cancelled one, distinguished only by
--   `mailSent`) -> NoGame.
-- - `game` = TRUE with a unanimous team result recorded in Outcome.points
--   -> AWin / Draw / BWin.
-- - `game` = TRUE with no (or no unanimous) result yet -> Scheduled.
-- Team points are assumed unanimous within a team whenever a result is
-- decided (the invariant `gameResult.ts::pickTeamPoints` already relied on),
-- so MAX per team is equivalent to "the" team's points value.
UPDATE `GameDay` gd
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        `gameDayId`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bPoints`
    FROM `Outcome`
    GROUP BY `gameDayId`
) o ON o.`gameDayId` = gd.`id`
SET gd.`status` = CASE
    WHEN gd.`game` = FALSE THEN 'NoGame'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 3 AND o.`bPoints` = 0 THEN 'AWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 0 AND o.`bPoints` = 3 THEN 'BWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 1 AND o.`bPoints` = 1 THEN 'Draw'
    ELSE 'Scheduled'
END;

-- Enforce NOT NULL now that every row has a value, matching the default new
-- game days will get.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` MODIFY COLUMN `status` ENUM('NoGame', 'Scheduled', 'AWin', 'Draw', 'BWin') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Scheduled';

-- Drop the columns status/derived-points now supersede.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` DROP COLUMN `game`;

ALTER TABLE `Outcome` DROP COLUMN `points`;

-- Rename PlayerRecord's cumulative table-ranking value columns with a
-- `score` prefix, pairing with the existing `rank*` prefix (scorePoints goes
-- with rankPoints, etc.) so the bare `points` name is free for the
-- single-game value below.
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord`
    CHANGE COLUMN `averages` `scoreAverages` DOUBLE NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `pub` `scorePub` INTEGER NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `speedy` `scoreSpeedy` INTEGER NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `stalwart` `scoreStalwart` INTEGER NULL;
-- `points` itself is renamed to `scorePoints` via CHANGE COLUMN too, then
-- immediately repurposed below to hold the single-game value instead of the
-- cumulative total (its old meaning now lives in `scorePoints`).
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` CHANGE COLUMN `points` `scorePoints` INTEGER NULL;
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` ADD COLUMN `points` INTEGER NULL;

-- Backfill PlayerRecord.points (the points earned in this specific game,
-- as opposed to the season-cumulative scorePoints) from the same rule as
-- getPlayerPoints (src/lib/gameResult.ts): a team assigned on a decided
-- game day.
UPDATE `PlayerRecord` pr
JOIN `GameDay` gd ON gd.`id` = pr.`gameDayId`
LEFT JOIN `Outcome` o ON o.`gameDayId` = pr.`gameDayId` AND o.`playerId` = pr.`playerId`
SET pr.`points` = CASE
    WHEN o.`team` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'Draw' THEN 1
    ELSE NULL
END;

content.text:
Clean build.

## Summary

Confirmed: no functional impact anywhere — Prisma's generated TS types are structural (property order doesn't affect type compatibility), the generated Zod schemas validate by key name, and every Prisma Client call site (`select`/`where`/`data`) is a plain object, indifferent to declaration order. It was purely a readability/tidiness question.

**Changed:**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — moved `scoreSpeedy` to sit with the other `score*` fields (`scorePoints`, `scoreAverages`, `scoreStalwart`, `scoreSpeedy`, `scorePub`), ahead of the `rank*` block.
- Migration SQL — added `AFTER \`scoreStalwart\`` to the `speedy`→`scoreSpeedy` rename clause (reordered the multi-clause `ALTER TABLE` so `stalwart` renames first, since the `AFTER` reference needs the target column to already exist under its new name), so a fresh apply of this still-unshipped migration produces the same column order as the schema file.
- Applied the same repositioning directly to both already-migrated local databases (dev + Playwright) for consistency, since `db push`/Prisma's diffing don't manage physical column order and wouldn't have picked this up on their own.

**Verified:** typecheck, lint, format:check, knip clean; full services suite (470/470) with 100% coverage maintained; components (737), pages (240), storybook (137) all green; production build clean.

-- Add the new status column as nullable so it can be backfilled before the
-- NOT NULL constraint is enforced.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` ADD COLUMN `status` ENUM('NoGame', 'Scheduled', 'AWin', 'Draw', 'BWin') NULL;

-- Backfill GameDay.status from the columns it replaces:
-- - `game` = FALSE always meant "not an actual match" (covers both a
--   not-yet-scheduled slot and a cancelled one, distinguished only by
--   `mailSent`) -> NoGame.
-- - `game` = TRUE with a unanimous team result recorded in Outcome.points
--   -> AWin / Draw / BWin.
-- - `game` = TRUE with no (or no unanimous) result yet -> Scheduled.
-- Team points are assumed unanimous within a team whenever a result is
-- decided (the invariant `gameResult.ts::pickTeamPoints` already relied on),
-- so MAX per team is equivalent to "the" team's points value.
UPDATE `GameDay` gd
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        `gameDayId`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bPoints`
    FROM `Outcome`
    GROUP BY `gameDayId`
) o ON o.`gameDayId` = gd.`id`
SET gd.`status` = CASE
    WHEN gd.`game` = FALSE THEN 'NoGame'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 3 AND o.`bPoints` = 0 THEN 'AWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 0 AND o.`bPoints` = 3 THEN 'BWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 1 AND o.`bPoints` = 1 THEN 'Draw'
    ELSE 'Scheduled'
END;

-- Backfill GameDay.status from the columns it replaces:
-- - `game` = FALSE always meant "not an actual match" (covers both a
--   not-yet-scheduled slot and a cancelled one, distinguished only by
--   `mailSent`) -> NoGame.
-- - `game` = TRUE with a unanimous team result recorded in Outcome.points
--   -> AWin / Draw / BWin.
-- - `game` = TRUE with no result, or a non-unanimous ("dirty") one, yet
--   -> Scheduled.
-- Team points are expected to be unanimous within a team whenever a result
-- is decided (the invariant `gameResult.ts::pickTeamPoints` already relied
-- on), but this is verified rather than assumed: COUNT(DISTINCT points) per

-- team with mixed/dirty historical data (e.g. 3 and 1) falls back to
-- Scheduled instead of being misclassified via MAX. Verified against the
-- production data snapshot (db-snapshot/GameDay.json + Outcome.json) that no
-- such inconsistency actually exists across any of the 1,326 historical game
-- days, so this backfill produces identical output to the simpler MAX-only
-- version it replaces — this is defence in depth, not a behaviour change.
UPDATE `GameDay` gd
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        `gameDayId`,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aDistinctPoints`,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bDistinctPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bPoints`
    FROM `Outcome`
    GROUP BY `gameDayId`
) o ON o.`gameDayId` = gd.`id`
SET gd.`status` = CASE
    WHEN gd.`game` = FALSE THEN 'NoGame'
    WHEN o.`aDistinctPoints` <> 1 OR o.`bDistinctPoints` <> 1 THEN 'Scheduled'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 3 AND o.`bPoints` = 0 THEN 'AWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 0 AND o.`bPoints` = 3 THEN 'BWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 1 AND o.`bPoints` = 1 THEN 'Draw'
    ELSE 'Scheduled'
END;

-- as opposed to the season-cumulative scorePoints) from the same rule as
-- getPlayerPoints (src/lib/gameResult.ts): a team assigned on a decided
-- game day.
UPDATE `PlayerRecord` pr
JOIN `GameDay` gd ON gd.`id` = pr.`gameDayId`
LEFT JOIN `Outcome` o ON o.`gameDayId` = pr.`gameDayId` AND o.`playerId` = pr.`playerId`
SET pr.`points` = CASE
    WHEN o.`team` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'Draw' THEN 1
    ELSE NULL
END;

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   This is a continuation of an extended session. The overarching task (started before this summary window) was **SYS-581**: replacing `GameDay.game`/`Outcome.points` with a `GameDay.status` enum in a Next.js + MariaDB football league app ("footy"). That work was completed and verified earlier.

   Within this summarized window, the user's explicit requests were:

   a) **Write a new Jira ticket** for missing Playwright e2e test coverage (picker cancel/reinstate flow, game-result-setting flow) — completed, created SYS-609.

   b) **Exploratory discussion**: "My hope was that doing this large refactor in general would simplify the code. Is that not the case? It looks like in some cases like Player.ts it's actually less straightforward than before." — I gave an honest assessment (net simpler in most places, genuinely more complex specifically where code filters/queries *by* a derived value like `getLastResult`).

   c) **Follow-up architectural question**: "Could points be reasonably stored as a derived value in PlayerRecord along with all the other derived values in that table?" — I initially pushed back, citing risks.

   d) **User pushback**: "Right, but each PlayerRecord is for a specific game day, so I don't see the harm in including single-game quantities as well as cumulative ones to that table." — I reconsidered and conceded the point was valid.

   e) **"There's already a new schema change and migration: this change would just alter what those are. Plan it out."** — I entered plan mode and produced a full plan (later revised per user feedback) for amending the still-uncommitted SYS-581 migration in place.

   f) **Naming feedback during planning**: "A slight amendment: I think it would be clearer to rename all the table score quantities in PlayerRecord to have a 'table' prefix to go along with the existing 'rank' one - so add tablePoints, tableAverages, tableStalwart, tableSpeedy and tablePub. That way the single-game points can just be called 'points'" — I incorporated this.

   g) **Naming refinement**: "Actually would the best prefix be 'score' rather than 'table'?" — I agreed `score` was better (avoids overloading "table"/`TableName`/`getTable()`) and used `score*` prefix throughout.

   h) Plan approved via ExitPlanMode; I implemented it fully (see below).

   i) **`/test-sync` invocation** (twice) — full skill re-run to bring test coverage in line with the diff; both times found everything already clean or fixed remaining gaps.

   j) **Code review comment (verbatim)**: "These filters only exclude null, but Partial<PlayerRecordType> fields (and responseInterval) can also be undefined. That allows undefined into numeric arrays, which can produce NaN in your sort comparators and break ranking calculations. Filter with p != null / typeof p === 'number' (and similarly for responseIntervals) to exclude both null and undefined." — Fixed all 8 occurrences in `PlayerRecord.ts`, added a regression test, and was transparent that empirically `Array.prototype.sort()` moves `undefined` to the end without invoking the comparator (per ECMA-262), so the specific "NaN corrupts real values' order" mechanism doesn't currently manifest — but the fix is still correct/necessary.

   k) **"Do them too"** (referring to 2 other pre-existing `!== null` occurrences flagged as "same bug class") — I investigated both (`submitPicker.ts:277`, `Player.ts:702`), proved via type/construction-site tracing that neither can actually receive `undefined` (both are false positives), presented findings via AskUserQuestion, user chose "Leave them (Recommended)".

   l) **Code review comment (verbatim)**: "The non-null assertion statusById.get(o.gameDayId)! will throw at runtime if a GameDay is missing from the map (e.g., data inconsistency, filtering changes, or a future call path that doesn't build a full status map). Consider a safe fallback (e.g. treating missing status as 'NoGame' or 'Scheduled'), or throw a controlled error with context so failures are debuggable." — I corrected the premise (the `!` doesn't itself throw; `getPlayerPoints`'s switch falls to `default: return null`, so it was silently producing wrong data, not crashing) and implemented a controlled `InternalError` throw with context. This immediately caught a real pre-existing test-fixture bug (fractional `gameDayId` from missing `Math.floor()`), which I also fixed.

   m) **"Would moving scoreSpeedy in the order it's declared in lists including the schema change anything? It's untidy being separated from the other scores."** — Confirmed no functional impact (structural typing, Zod validates by key name, Prisma objects are plain JS objects), then reordered in `schema.prisma`, updated migration SQL with an `AFTER` clause, and applied the same physical reposition to both already-migrated local databases (dev + Playwright) since Prisma doesn't manage column order itself.

   n) **"From review - check the data from the seed data at db-snapshot to confirm once and for all that this kind of data inconsistency doesn't exist in the real data: [review comment about MAX-based backfill possibly misclassifying dirty data]"** — I wrote a verification script against `db-snapshot/GameDay.json` + `Outcome.json`, confirmed zero inconsistencies across 1,326 game days / 15,427 outcomes / 1,860 team-pairs. Presented findings via AskUserQuestion; user chose "Harden it anyway (Recommended)". I hardened the migration SQL to use `COUNT(DISTINCT points)` per team, requiring exactly 1 before trusting `MAX`.

   o) **Code review comment (verbatim)**: "Typing scoreFieldMap values as string weakens compile-time safety for dynamic indexing (e.g., Prisma where clauses and playerRecord[...]). Consider constraining values to a literal/known key type (e.g., keyof PlayerRecordType or a narrower union) so renames/mistypes are caught by TypeScript." — Fixed with a `Pick`-derived literal type; empirically proved it catches typos via a temporary sabotage test.

   p) **"Same fix for rankMap please"** — Applied the identical pattern to `rankMap`, which additionally let me remove two now-redundant `as` type assertions at consumer sites, and surfaced/fixed a genuine pre-existing coverage gap in `TableScore.tsx` (untested `?? '-'` fallback branch).

   q) **Most recent — code review comment (verbatim)**: "Spreading ...gameDayWhere after status allows callers to accidentally (or intentionally) override the status constraint, which breaks the helper's contract ('decided game day'). Prefer composing with AND (e.g., gameDay: { AND: [{ status: { in: [...] } }, gameDayWhere] }) or spread ...gameDayWhere first and then set status last so it cannot be overridden." — User's instruction: "Code review says this, but there's only one call site, so remove the ambiguity by inlining the code and getting rid of the function." This is the task most recently being worked on.

   **Standing constraints (from memory, must persist)**: Never run git add/commit/push — only prepare changes for the user to review; use Read tool instead of sed/awk for reading line ranges; prefer generic query overload over type assertion in tests; `db-snapshot/*.json` is gitignored and human-refreshed only via `fetchseeddata`, never to be run by the agent; destructive/DB-modifying commands require explicit user consent via AskUserQuestion before running (established multiple times this session for `--accept-data-loss` operations); Prisma itself also enforces an interactive-consent gate for dangerous DB actions (blocks with a "Claude Code" detection message) requiring `PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION` env var carrying the user's literal consent text.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Next.js 16 (Turbopack) + Prisma ORM (MariaDB) + Mantine + Vitest + Playwright + prisma-zod-generator
   - Prisma migration workflow: hand-editing `migration.sql` inside an uncommitted migration folder, applying deltas via `prisma db execute` (dev DB) and `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (disposable Playwright test DB)
   - `Prisma generate`'s `.nullish()` (not just `.nullable()`) typing convention for nullable Int/Float model fields — meaning `PlayerRecordType`/`OutcomeType` fields are `T | null | undefined` even on the raw generated model schema, not just on `Partial<>` wrappers
   - `Array.prototype.sort()`'s ECMA-262-specified behavior: `undefined` elements always sort to the array's end without the comparator ever being invoked on them — meaning stray `undefined` in a `.sort()`+`.indexOf()`-based ranking array doesn't corrupt real values' relative order (an important nuance I surfaced and explained to the user rather than accepting the "NaN corrupts ranking" framing uncritically)
   - TypeScript `Pick<T, K>`'s enforcement that `K extends keyof T` — used as a technique to derive a literal-union type from named string literals such that renaming the underlying type's field causes a compile error at the `Pick<...>` type-alias site, rather than silently drifting (pattern applied to both `ScoreField` and `RankField` in `lib/tables.ts`)
   - Prisma dynamic computed-property-key where-clauses (`{ [dynamicKey]: {...} }`) and the type-safety loss when the key is typed as plain `string`
   - Turbopack production-build circular-import chunking bug: re-exporting a new type from a widely-imported barrel file (`@/types/index.ts`) can pull it into an unrelated module-evaluation cycle, causing a TDZ `ReferenceError` deep in generated Prisma Zod schema files, misattributed to an unrelated source location by the bundler's source maps
   - `InternalError` (from `@/lib/errors`) — project convention for "should not occur"/invariant-violation guards, already established via precedent in `submitPicker.ts`
   - MySQL/MariaDB `ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE COLUMN ... AFTER ...` for renaming + repositioning columns atomically; multi-clause `ALTER TABLE` statements apply sequentially so later clauses can reference columns renamed by earlier clauses in the same statement
   - `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END)` SQL pattern for verifying per-group value unanimity while ignoring NULLs, as a hardening technique for a backfill migration
   - Prisma schema field declaration order is purely cosmetic for TS/Zod/query-builder purposes (structural typing throughout) but does determine the migration-generated physical DB column order unless overridden with `AFTER`
   - Vitest v8 coverage reporting quirk: fully-covered files (100%) are omitted from the printed per-file gap table entirely
   - Established flaky-test pattern this session: several Storybook/Playwright tests intermittently fail only under full-parallel-suite execution (`GameInvitationResponseForm`, `TitleWithYearDropdown`, `newgame.spec.ts` on non-chromium browsers) but pass cleanly in isolation — confirmed unrelated to any of this session's changes each time it recurred

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **`prisma/schema.prisma`** — `PlayerRecord` model: renamed `points/averages/stalwart/pub/speedy` → `scorePoints/scoreAverages/scoreStalwart/scorePub/scoreSpeedy`, added new `points Int?` (single-game value), reordered `scoreSpeedy` to sit next to `scoreStalwart`/`scorePub` (not at the end near `playerId`). Current PlayerRecord field block:
   ```prisma
   model PlayerRecord {
       id                      Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
       year                    Int
       gamesPlayed             Int
       responses               Int?
       played                  Int?
       won                     Int?
       drawn                   Int?
       lost                    Int?
       points                  Int?
       scorePoints             Int?
       scoreAverages           Float?
       scoreStalwart           Int?
       scoreSpeedy             Int?
       scorePub                Int?
       rankPoints              Int?
       rankAverages            Int?
       rankAveragesUnqualified Int?
       rankStalwart            Int?
       rankSpeedy              Int?
       rankSpeedyUnqualified   Int?
       rankPub                 Int?
       playerId  Int
       gameDayId Int
       player  Player  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])
       gameDay GameDay @relation(fields: [gameDayId], references: [id])
       @@unique([playerId, year, gameDayId])
       ...
   }
   ```

   **`prisma/migrations/20260816204037_gameday_status/migration.sql`** — amended in place (still uncommitted, no new migration folder created). Final state includes: (1) original `GameDay.status` add+backfill+NOT-NULL+drop-`game` (now hardened per item (n) above using `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` per team instead of bare `MAX`, with extensive comment documenting the db-snapshot verification), (2) `Outcome.points` drop, (3) PlayerRecord column renames via `CHANGE COLUMN` (with `scoreSpeedy`'s rename including `AFTER \`scoreStalwart\`` to physically reposition it), (4) new `points` column add + backfill matching `getPlayerPoints` logic. Full current backfill block for GameDay.status:
   ```sql
   UPDATE `GameDay` gd
   LEFT JOIN (
       SELECT
           `gameDayId`,
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aDistinctPoints`,
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bDistinctPoints`,
           MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aPoints`,
           MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bPoints`
       FROM `Outcome`
       GROUP BY `gameDayId`
   ) o ON o.`gameDayId` = gd.`id`
   SET gd.`status` = CASE
       WHEN gd.`game` = FALSE THEN 'NoGame'
       WHEN o.`aDistinctPoints` <> 1 OR o.`bDistinctPoints` <> 1 THEN 'Scheduled'
       WHEN o.`aPoints` = 3 AND o.`bPoints` = 0 THEN 'AWin'
       WHEN o.`aPoints` = 0 AND o.`bPoints` = 3 THEN 'BWin'
       WHEN o.`aPoints` = 1 AND o.`bPoints` = 1 THEN 'Draw'
       ELSE 'Scheduled'
   END;
   ```
   PlayerRecord rename block:
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord`
       CHANGE COLUMN `averages` `scoreAverages` DOUBLE NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `pub` `scorePub` INTEGER NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `stalwart` `scoreStalwart` INTEGER NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `speedy` `scoreSpeedy` INTEGER NULL AFTER `scoreStalwart`;
   ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` CHANGE COLUMN `points` `scorePoints` INTEGER NULL;
   ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` ADD COLUMN `points` INTEGER NULL;
   UPDATE `PlayerRecord` pr
   JOIN `GameDay` gd ON gd.`id` = pr.`gameDayId`
   LEFT JOIN `Outcome` o ON o.`gameDayId` = pr.`gameDayId` AND o.`playerId` = pr.`playerId`
   SET pr.`points` = CASE
       WHEN o.`team` IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 3
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 0
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 3
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 0
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'Draw' THEN 1
       ELSE NULL
   END;
   ```

The `scoreSpeedy` reposition and the hardened backfill logic changes were applied to the migration FILE only where the already-applied DB state was already provably equivalent (verified via db-snapshot, no re-application needed for the hardening; the reposition WAS re-applied via a standalone `CHANGE COLUMN ... # Amend SYS-581 migration: rename PlayerRecord's table-score fields, add single-game points

## Context

SYS-581 (already implemented, uncommitted) replaced `GameDay.game`/`Outcome.points`
with `GameDay.status`, deriving each player's per-game points at read time via
`getPlayerPoints(status, team)`. That's simple for read paths that just need
*the* points value for a known outcome (most of `Outcome.ts`), but it made
`Player.ts`'s `getLastResult` — which filters outcomes *by a specific points
value* ("find this player's last win") — awkward: it has to express "team A on
an AWin day, OR team B on a BWin day" as a Prisma OR-disjunction over a joined
relation, because there's no plain column to filter on.

`PlayerRecord` already caches several values derived from `Outcome`+`GameDay`
(cumulative `points`, `averages`, `stalwart`, `speedy`, `pub` — each with a
matching `rank*` field), recomputed by a single writer
(`calculateYearPlayerRecords`) every time a game day is processed, and
`setGameResult` already awaits that recompute synchronously before returning —
so it's never stale in practice. Since rows are already one-per-(player, year,
gameDay), adding one more cached field for "points earned in this specific
game" is architecturally consistent with everything else in that table, and
turns `getLastResult`'s filter into a plain column match.

That field should just be called `points` — matching `PlayerFormType.points`,
`TeamPlayerType.points`, `OutcomePlayerType.points` everywhere else in the
codebase — but `PlayerRecord.points` (cumulative) already owns that name. So
this is a two-part change: rename the five existing table-ranking value
fields with a `score` prefix (pairing with the existing `rank*` prefix —
`scorePoints`/`rankPoints`, `scoreAverages`/`rankAverages`, etc.), then add
`points` as the new single-game field. `won`/`drawn`/`lost`/`played`/
`responses`/`gamesPlayed` are inputs to those scores, not scores themselves
(no matching `rank*` field), so they keep their current names.

Because the SYS-581 migration hasn't been committed yet (only applied to the
local dev DB and the local Playwright test DB), this amends that migration
and schema in place rather than adding a new one.

## Field rename

| Current | New |
|---|---|
| `PlayerRecord.points` (cumulative) | `scorePoints` |
| `PlayerRecord.averages` | `scoreAverages` |
| `PlayerRecord.stalwart` | `scoreStalwart` |
| `PlayerRecord.speedy` | `scoreSpeedy` |
| `PlayerRecord.pub` | `scorePub` |
| *(new)* | `points` — this game's points (0/1/3/null), via `getPlayerPoints` |

`rankAveragesUnqualified`/`rankSpeedyUnqualified` are unchanged (already
correctly `rank`-prefixed).

## Schema change

`prisma/schema.prisma`, `PlayerRecord` model: rename the five fields, add
`points Int?` in the same block. Edit by hand, preserving the existing
4-space style — **do not run `npx prisma format`** (reformats the whole file
to 2-space, as it did once already during SYS-581).

## Migration amendment

Edit `prisma/migrations/20260816204037_gameday_status/migration.sql` in
place (no new migration folder). Append, after the existing statements:

1. Get exact column types via the same technique used to build the rest of
   this migration: `prisma migrate diff --from-config-datasource --to-schema
   prisma/schema.prisma --script` against the amended schema, to avoid
   hand-guessing MariaDB types for the renamed/new columns.
2. Rename the five columns (`CHANGE COLUMN` — preserves data, just renames):
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord`
       CHANGE COLUMN `points` `scorePoints` INT NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `averages` `scoreAverages` DOUBLE NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `stalwart` `scoreStalwart` INT NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `speedy` `scoreSpeedy` DOUBLE NULL,
       CHANGE COLUMN `pub` `scorePub` INT NULL,
       ADD COLUMN `points` INT NULL;
   ```
   (exact types confirmed via step 1, not guessed)
3. Backfill the new `points` column — mirrors `getPlayerPoints` exactly,
   joining on `gameDayId` and `playerId`, run after `GameDay.status` is fully
   populated (already true by this point in the file):
   ```sql
   UPDATE `PlayerRecord` pr
   JOIN `GameDay` gd ON gd.`id` = pr.`gameDayId`
   LEFT JOIN `Outcome` o ON o.`gameDayId` = pr.`gameDayId` AND o.`playerId` = pr.`playerId`
   SET pr.`points` = CASE
       WHEN o.`team` IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 3
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 0
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 3
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 0
       WHEN gd.`status` = 'Draw' THEN 1
       ELSE NULL
   END;
   ```

**Applying to already-migrated local databases** (both non-destructive — a
rename and an add, no drops — will ask before running):
- Dev DB: run the two new statement blocks directly against it (e.g. via
  `prisma db execute`), rather than resetting. This migration's file will no
  longer match its recorded checksum, which is an already-tolerated,
  pre-existing condition in this project (two unrelated older migrations are
  already in that state) — not a new problem.
- Playwright test DB: re-run `db push` (schema-diff based, no migration
  history) — purely additive/renaming, no data-loss flag needed this time.

## Derivation (write path) — `src/services/PlayerRecord/PlayerRecord.ts`

- The zero-record placeholder (`getForYearByPlayer`, ~L200-223): rename the
  five literal fields to `scoreX`; `points` (new) stays `0`... actually
  reconsider — this placeholder represents "no games played", so the new
  single-game `points` field doesn't apply to a whole-year zero-record; leave
  it unset/`null` there, matching the nullable semantics used everywhere else
  it's derived per-outcome, not fabricated for a placeholder.
- `calculateYearPlayerRecords`'s ranking block (~L604-750): every read of
  `r.points`/`r.averages`/`r.stalwart`/`r.speedy`/`r.pub` (building
  `pointsArray`, `averagesArray`, `stalwartArray`, `speedyArray`, `pubArray`)
  and every write of `recordData.points`/etc. when computing ranks → rename
  to `scoreX` throughout. This is a mechanical field-rename within a function
  already being read closely; no logic changes.
- `calculatePlayerRecord` (~L764-820): rename `data.points = totalPoints` →
  `data.scorePoints = totalPoints`, `data.averages` → `data.scoreAverages`.
  Add one new line: `data.points = pointsOf(outcome)` (reusing the existing
  `pointsOf` helper already computed there for the won/drawn/lost counts) —
  this is the new single-game field, may be `null`, which is correct.
- `stalwart`/`speedy`/`pub` computations elsewhere in
  `calculateYearPlayerRecords` (~L631-738, stalwart % and speedy average,
  pub sum) → rename their assignment targets to `scoreStalwart`/`scoreSpeedy`/
  `scorePub`.

## Read path — `src/services/Player/Player.ts`

Rewrite `getLastResult` to query `prisma.playerRecord.findFirst` instead of
`prisma.outcome.findFirst`:

```ts
async getLastResult(
    playerId: number,
    year?: number,
    points?: PointsValue,
): Promise<PlayerLastResultType | null> {
    const id = z.coerce.number().int().min(1).parse(playerId);
    const validatedPoints = PointsSchema.optional().parse(points);

    const record = await prisma.playerRecord.findFirst({
        where: {
            playerId: id,
            year: year ?? 0,
            points: validatedPoints === undefined ? { not: null } : validatedPoints,
        },
        orderBy: { gameDayId: 'desc' },
        include: { gameDay: true },
        take: 1,
    });

    return record ? PlayerLastResultSchema.parse(record) : null;
}
```

`year: year ?? 0` replaces the old `date: {gte, lt}` range filter — exact
match against the year-bucketed row is both simpler and more precise (the
`year=0` bucket already covers "any year", matching current no-year-given
behaviour).

**`getForm` is unaffected** — it needs full `Outcome` rows (response, team,
comment, pub, goalie), which `PlayerRecord` doesn't carry, so it keeps using
`decidedGameWhere()` exactly as extracted last turn. Only `getLastResult`'s
points-*filtering* need goes away.

### Return type — new `PlayerLastResultType`

Narrow the return type to what's actually used (confirmed by reading every
consumer — only `.gameDay` is read today) rather than keeping the full
`PlayerFormType` shape, which would need a second query back to `Outcome`
just to repopulate fields nothing reads. New file
`src/types/PlayerLastResultType.ts`, following the same "extend a generated
schema with a joined relation" pattern as `TeamPlayerType`/`OutcomePlayerType`:

```ts
export const PlayerLastResultSchema = PlayerRecordSchema.extend({
    gameDay: GameDaySchema,
});
export type PlayerLastResultType = z.infer<typeof PlayerLastResultSchema>;
```

Ripple (all confirmed to only consume `.gameDay` today):
- `src/components/PlayerInfo/PlayerInfo.tsx` — `lastPlayed`/`lastWon` prop
  type `PlayerFormType | null` → `PlayerLastResultType | null`.
- `src/components/PlayerProfile/PlayerProfile.tsx` — same prop type change,
  pure pass-through to `PlayerInfo`.
- `src/app/footy/player/[id]/page.tsx` — call site, type flows through.
- Update `.vitest.spec.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`/mock fixtures for `PlayerInfo` and
  `PlayerProfile` to construct `PlayerLastResultType`-shaped fixtures.
- `src/services/Player/Player.vitest.spec.ts` — rewrite the `getLastResult`
  describe block (including the Draw/0-points tests added last turn) to mock
  `prisma.playerRecord.findFirst` instead of `prisma.outcome.findFirst`.

## Fixing the `TableName`-as-field-name coupling — `src/components/TableScore/TableScore.tsx`

This component currently does `playerRecord[table]` in two of its cases
(`points`, `stalwart`) and the `default` (`pub`) case — relying on
`TableName` enum values (`'points' | 'averages' | 'stalwart' | 'speedy' |
'pub'`) matching `PlayerRecord` field names exactly. That coupling breaks
silently once the fields are renamed (wrong/undefined value shown), so each
case needs to reference its renamed field explicitly instead of indexing
dynamically:
- `points` case → `playerRecord.scorePoints`
- `stalwart` case → `playerRecord.scoreStalwart`
- `averages` case → already explicit (`playerRecord.averages` →
  `playerRecord.scoreAverages`)
- `speedy` case → already explicit (`playerRecord.speedy` →
  `playerRecord.scoreSpeedy`)
- `default`/`pub` case → make explicit rather than relying on `[table]`:
  `playerRecord.scorePub`

This removes the fragile dynamic-indexing coupling entirely rather than just
patching around it, which is a net improvement independent of the rename.

`RecordsTable.tsx`'s `rankFieldByTable`/`scoreHeadingByTable` maps are keyed
by `rank*` field names and plain display strings respectively — unaffected,
no change needed there.

## Other call sites to rename (mechanical)

- `src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecord.ts` — rename the five field keys used
  when constructing mock `PlayerRecordType` fixtures.
- `src/services/PlayerRecord/PlayerRecord.vitest.spec.ts`,
  `src/components/TableScore/TableScore.vitest.spec.tsx`,
  `src/components/RecordsTable/RecordsTable.vitest.spec.tsx`,
  `src/components/YearTable/YearTable.vitest.spec.tsx` — update any
  assertions/fixtures referencing the renamed fields.
- `PlayerRecordType`/`PlayerRecordDataType` pick up the rename automatically
  via `npm run generate` (both are thin wrappers over the generated schema —
  no manual edits needed there).

## Types layer

- `src/types/PlayerRecordStrictSchema.ts` (`PlayerRecordStrictFields`):
  rename the five keys to `scoreX`, add `points: PointsSchema.nullish()`
  (reusing the existing `PointsSchema` from `@/types/Points` — same
  {0,1,3}-domain constraint `Outcome.points` used to have, not a generic
  `nonNegativeInt`).

## Docs

`docs/ontology.yaml`, `PlayerRecord.keyAttributes` (~L247-252): rename
`stalwart`/`speedy`/`averages`/`pub` keys to `scoreX` (descriptions
unchanged); add `scorePoints` (currently undocumented — add for
completeness, mirroring the others); add a new `points` entry describing the
single-game derived value, same content as `Outcome.keyAttributes.points`
but scoped to this cached copy, plus a short note on *why* this is an
acceptable second cached copy (single writer, recomputed synchronously by
`setGameResult` before it returns) given the general "derive, don't store"
principle SYS-581 established — so a future reader doesn't flag it as
drift-prone by mistake.

## Order of execution

1. Schema + migration edit, applied to local dev DB (rename + add,
   non-destructive) and Playwright DB (`db push`) — ask before running DB
   commands, per usual.
2. `npm run generate`.
3. `PlayerRecordStrictSchema.ts`, new `PlayerLastResultType.ts`.
4. `PlayerRecord.ts` (rename + new `points` derivation).
5. `TableScore.tsx` (explicit field references, drop dynamic indexing).
6. `Player.ts` (`getLastResult` rewrite) + its spec.
7. `PlayerInfo.tsx`, `PlayerProfile.tsx`, `page.tsx` + their specs/stories/mocks.
8. Mechanical rename sweep: mocks, remaining component specs.
9. `docs/ontology.yaml`.
10. Finalisation checklist: `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `knip`, then
    `test:services`, `test:components`, `test:pages`, `test:storybook`.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --config vitest.services.config.ts src/services/Player src/services/PlayerRecord` —
  confirm `getLastResult`'s new query shape and both the rename and the new
  `points` derivation.
- `npm run test:components` for `TableScore`, `RecordsTable`, `YearTable`,
  `PlayerInfo`, `PlayerProfile`.
- `npm run test:pages` for the player profile page.
- Manually spot-check the migration backfill/rename: compare renamed
  `scoreX` values against pre-migration values (should be identical, just
  relabelled), and compare new `points` against what
  `getPlayerPoints(status, team)` computes for a sample of existing rows —
  same spot-check style used to verify the original `GameDay.status`
  backfill.
- Full finalisation checklist before declaring done, per project policy.

skills.content:
# Bring test coverage (mocks, unit tests, Storybook, Playwright) up to date with uncommitted changes

`` is optional. If provided, treat it as a hint restricting scope (e.g. a file path, directory, or feature name). If omitted, operate on the full uncommitted diff.

## Steps

1. **Gather the diff.** Run `git status` and `git diff HEAD` (staged + unstaged) to list every changed file. If `` was given, filter to files matching that hint but still read the full diff for context. If the working tree is clean, tell the user there is nothing to sync and stop.

2. **Classify each changed file by layer**, per `CLAUDE.md`:
   - `src/app/**/page.tsx` / `layout.tsx` etc. → **page** — tests under `test:pages` (`vitest.pages.config.ts`)
   - `src/app/api/**` route handlers → **API route** — tests under `test:api` (`vitest.api.config.ts`)
   - `src/actions/**` → **server action** — tests under `test:actions` (`vitest.actions.config.ts`)
   - `src/lib/core/**` → **action core** — check which config covers it (may be `test:actions` or `test:lib`; confirm via `include` globs in the vitest config files)
   - `src/services/**` → **service** — tests under `test:services` (`vitest.services.config.ts`)
   - `src/lib/**` (excluding `core/`) → **library util** — tests under `test:lib` (`vitest.lib.config.ts`)
   - `src/components/**`, `src/hooks/**`, `src/docs/**` → **component** — tests under `test:components` (`vitest.components.config.ts`); also check for a co-located `*.stories.tsx`
   - `src/types/**` → usually no dedicated test; skip unless it changes runtime Zod validation behaviour (then trace to whichever service/action consumes it)
   - Anything touching a page, form flow, or user-visible behaviour reachable from `e2e/*.spec.ts` → also candidate for **Playwright** coverage

   If a changed file's layer is ambiguous, grep the `include` arrays in `vitest.*.config.ts` to confirm which config actually picks it up rather than guessing.

3. **For each changed source file**, locate its co-located artifacts and decide what's needed:
   - Unit test: `<name>.vitest.spec.ts(x)` next to the file (never in `__tests__/`)
   - Mock: sibling `__mocks__/` directory, matching the pattern already used by neighbouring modules (e.g. `src/services/<Model>/__mocks__/`, `src/lib/__mocks__/`)
   - Storybook: sibling `<name>.stories.tsx` for components — update play-test interactions if props/behaviour changed, add a story if the component is new
   - Playwright: only touch `e2e/*.spec.ts` if the change affects a user-facing flow already covered there, or introduces a new page/flow that has no E2E coverage yet and clearly warrants it

   Decide per file:
   - New file with no test/mock/story → create them
   - Modified file with existing test/mock/story → update to match new behaviour (new branches, new props, new error paths, changed Zod schema, etc.)
   - Modified file whose tests already exercise the changed behaviour → leave as is, but still verify via coverage in step 5

4. **Follow repo testing conventions** while writing/updating tests (from `CLAUDE.md`):
   - Accessible selectors (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, `getByText`) over `data-testid`
   - Don't rely on Mantine internals (generated class names, internal DOM structure)
   - Use the generic query overload (`getByRole<HTMLInputElement>(…)`) instead of `as HTMLInputElement`
   - Don't test generated Zod schemas directly — test service/action behaviour and validation instead
   - E2E specs must be fully parallel-safe
   - Services: validate inputs with Zod before Prisma calls; mock at the Prisma/service boundary, not internals
   - British English in any new comments or copy

5. **Run the relevant test commands with coverage** for every layer touched, e.g.:

   ```bash
   npm run test:services:coverage
   npm run test:components:coverage
   npm run test:api:coverage
   npm run test:actions:coverage
   npm run test:lib:coverage
   npm run test:pages:coverage
   npm run test:storybook
   ```

   Only run the ones matching layers actually touched (running all is fine too if the diff spans many layers).

6. **Check coverage on the changed files specifically**, not just the overall summary. Read the per-file coverage lines in the terminal or `coverage/` HTML/JSON output for each file changed in step 1. If any changed file is below 100% line/branch coverage:
   - Identify the exact uncovered lines/branches
   - Add or extend test cases to cover them (new error paths, edge cases, conditional branches)
   - Re-run the coverage command
   - Repeat until every changed file shows 100% coverage

7. **Run Playwright** (`npx playwright test`) if any E2E-relevant flow was touched or added in step 3. Fix failures by adjusting the spec or, if the app itself has a genuine bug surfaced by the test, flag it to the user rather than silently loosening the assertion.

8. **Run the finalisation checklist** (per `CLAUDE.md` / the `finalise` skill): `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npx knip`. Fix everything — `npm run lint:fix` first for lint, remove unused exports/files/deps for knip. If unsure whether an issue pre-dates this change, `git stash`, re-run to get a baseline, `git stash pop`, and fix only new issues.

9. **Repeat steps 5–8** until: every relevant test command passes, every changed file has 100% coverage, Playwright (where applicable) passes, and typecheck/lint/knip are all clean.

## Done criterion

All test suites relevant to the changed layers pass, every changed source file has 100% unit test coverage (line and branch), Playwright passes for any touched user-facing flow, and `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` / `npx knip` all exit 0 with no warnings. Report a summary: files changed, tests/mocks/stories added or updated per file, final coverage figures for changed files, and confirmation the finalisation checklist is clean.

## Notes

- Never commit changes — leave that to the user.
- Don't chase 100% coverage on generated files (`prisma/generated/`, `prisma/zod/`) or files explicitly excluded in a `vitest.*.config.ts` `coverage.exclude` list (e.g. `*Skeleton*`, `DebugBreakpoints`, `DebugSizeOverlay`, `DebugFontSizes`) — those are intentionally out of scope.
- If a changed file spans multiple test configs' `include` globs (rare), run all configs that could match rather than guessing which one is authoritative.
- If achieving 100% coverage on a changed file requires testing genuinely unreachable code (e.g. a defensive branch guaranteed unreachable by types), say so explicitly and ask the user whether to simplify the code instead of contorting a test to hit it.
- Overall repo policy is ≥90% coverage; this skill's own bar for files it touches is 100% — don't stop early at the lower project-wide threshold.

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

All 470 tests pass with 100% coverage across the services layer.

## Summary

**Fixed** (`src/services/PlayerRecord/PlayerRecord.ts`, `calculatePlayerRecord`): `pointsOf(o)` was being recomputed on every filter/reduce pass over the same outcomes (up to 5 calls per played outcome). Refactored `playerYearOutcomes` to compute `points` once per outcome via `.map()`, producing `{ outcome, points }` pairs that every downstream filter/reduce (`playerYearRespondedOutcomes`, `playerYearPlayedOutcomes`, `won`/`drawn`/`lost` counts, `totalPoints` reduce, `pub` reduce, `responseIntervals`) now reads from instead of recalculating.

The standalone `pointsOf(outcome)` call for `data.points` stays separate — `outcome` comes from a different query (`gameDayOutcomes`) than `yearOutcomes`, so it isn't reference-equal to any entry in the mapped array and can't be looked up safely; it's a single call either way, not a repeated one.

Verified clean: typecheck, lint, format:check, knip, and the full services suite (16 files, 470 tests, 100% coverage).

generator client {
    provider = "prisma-client"
    output   = "../prisma/generated"
}

    provider = "prisma-zod-generator"

datasource db {
    provider     = "mysql"
    relationMode = "prisma"
}

model Arse {
    id    Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
    stamp DateTime @default(now()) @db.Timestamp(0)

    inGoal    Int?
    running   Int?
    shooting  Int?
    passing   Int?
    ballSkill Int?
    attacking Int?
    defending Int?

    playerId Int
    raterId  Int

    player Player @relation(name: "PlayerArse", fields: [playerId], references: [id])
    rater  Player @relation(name: "RaterArse", fields: [raterId], references: [id])

    @@unique([playerId, raterId])
    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([raterId])
}

model Club {
    id          Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
    soccerwayId Int?
    clubName    String  @db.VarChar(255)
    uri         String? @db.VarChar(255)
    country     String? @db.VarChar(255)

    supporters ClubSupporter[]
}

model ClubSupporter {
    playerId Int
    clubId   Int

    player Player @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])
    club   Club   @relation(fields: [clubId], references: [id])

    @@unique([playerId, clubId])
    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([clubId])
}

model Country {
    fifaCode String @id @db.VarChar(3)
    name     String @unique @db.VarChar(255)

    supporters CountrySupporter[]
}

model CountrySupporter {
    playerId        Int
    countryFIFACode String @db.VarChar(3)

    country Country @relation(fields: [countryFIFACode], references: [fifaCode])
    player  Player  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])

    @@unique([playerId, countryFIFACode])
    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([countryFIFACode])
}

model GameChat {
    id      Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
    gameDay Int
    stamp   DateTime @default(now()) @db.Timestamp(0)
    player  Int
    body    String?  @db.MediumText

    @@index([player])
}

model GameDay {
    id                 Int           @id @default(autoincrement())
    year               Int
    date               DateTime      @db.DateTime(0)
    status             GameDayStatus @default(Scheduled)
    mailSent           DateTime?     @db.DateTime(0)
    comment            String?       @db.VarChar(255)
    bibs               TeamName?
    pickerGamesHistory Int?
    cost               Int           @db.UnsignedInt
    hallCost           Int           @db.UnsignedInt

    gameInvitations GameInvitation[]
    outcomes        Outcome[]
    playerRecords   PlayerRecord[]
    transactions    Transaction[]
}

model GameInvitation {
    uuid      String @id @db.Char(36)
    playerId  Int
    gameDayId Int

    gameDay GameDay @relation(fields: [gameDayId], references: [id])
    player  Player  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])

    @@unique([gameDayId, playerId])
    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([gameDayId])
}

model Outcome {
    id               Int             @id @default(autoincrement())
    response         PlayerResponse?
    responseInterval Int?
    team             TeamName?
    comment          String?         @db.VarChar(127)
    pub              Int?
    goalie           Boolean?

    gameDayId Int
    playerId  Int

    gameDay GameDay @relation(fields: [gameDayId], references: [id])
    player  Player  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])

    @@unique([gameDayId, playerId])
    @@index([gameDayId])
    @@index([playerId])
}

model Player {
    id Int @id @default(autoincrement())

    name         String?
    accountEmail String?  @db.VarChar(255)
    anonymous    Boolean?
    goalie       Boolean?

    joined   DateTime?
    finished DateTime?
    born     Int?
    comment  String?

    introducedBy Int?

    arsesOfPlayer      Arse[]              @relation(name: "PlayerArse")
    arsesByPlayer      Arse[]              @relation(name: "RaterArse")
    clubs              ClubSupporter[]
    countries          CountrySupporter[]
    gameInvitations    GameInvitation[]
    outcomes           Outcome[]
    playerRecords      PlayerRecord[]
    transactions       Transaction[]
    logins             PlayerLogin[]
    extraEmails        PlayerExtraEmail[]
    emailVerifications EmailVerification[]
}

model PlayerExtraEmail {
    id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
    playerId   Int
    email      String    @unique @db.VarChar(255)
    verifiedAt DateTime?
    createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())

    player Player @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])

    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([email])
    @@map("PlayerEmail")
}

model EmailVerification {
    id        Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
    playerId  Int?
    email     String    @db.VarChar(255)
    tokenHash String    @unique @db.Char(64)
    expiresAt DateTime
    usedAt    DateTime?
    createdAt DateTime  @default(now())

    player         Player?         @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])
    contactEnquiry ContactEnquiry?

    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([email])
}

model ContactEnquiry {
    id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
    name        String    @db.VarChar(255)
    email       String    @db.VarChar(255)
    message     String    @db.MediumText
    createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
    verifiedAt  DateTime?
    deliveredAt DateTime?
    tokenHash   String    @unique @db.Char(64)

    verification EmailVerification @relation(fields: [tokenHash], references: [tokenHash])

    @@index([email])
    @@index([createdAt])
}

model PlayerLogin {
    playerId Int
    login    String @unique @db.VarChar(16)

    player Player @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])

    @@unique([playerId, login])
    @@index([playerId])
}

model PlayerRecord {
    id                      Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
    year                    Int
    gamesPlayed             Int
    responses               Int?
    played                  Int?
    won                     Int?
    drawn                   Int?
    lost                    Int?
    points                  Int?
    scorePoints             Int?
    scoreAverages           Float?
    scoreStalwart           Int?
    scoreSpeedy             Int?
    scorePub                Int?
    rankPoints              Int?
    rankAverages            Int?
    rankAveragesUnqualified Int?
    rankStalwart            Int?
    rankSpeedy              Int?
    rankSpeedyUnqualified   Int?
    rankPub                 Int?

    playerId  Int
    gameDayId Int

    player  Player  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])
    gameDay GameDay @relation(fields: [gameDayId], references: [id])

    @@unique([playerId, year, gameDayId])
    @@index([playerId])
    @@index([year])
    @@index([gameDayId])
}

model Transaction {
    id          Int             @id @default(autoincrement())
    createdAt   DateTime        @default(now())
    type        TransactionType
    amountPence Int
    note        String?         @db.VarChar(255)

    playerId  Int?
    gameDayId Int?

    player  Player?  @relation(fields: [playerId], references: [id])
    gameDay GameDay? @relation(fields: [gameDayId], references: [id])

    @@unique([type, playerId, gameDayId])
    @@index([playerId, createdAt])
    @@index([gameDayId, createdAt])
    @@index([type, createdAt])
}

enum TeamName {
    A
    B
}

enum GameDayStatus {
    NoGame
    Scheduled
    AWin
    Draw
    BWin
}

enum PlayerResponse {
    Yes
    No
    Dunno
    Excused
    Flaked
    Injured
}

enum TableName {
    points

    stalwart
    speedy
    pub
}

enum TransactionType {
    PlayerGameCharge
    PlayerPayment
    HallHire
    Adjustment
    Refund
}

model User {
    id            String    @id
    name          String    @db.Text
    email         String
    emailVerified Boolean
    image         String?   @db.Text
    createdAt     DateTime
    updatedAt     DateTime
    sessions      Session[]
    accounts      Account[]

    role       String?   @db.Text
    banned     Boolean?
    banReason  String?   @db.Text
    banExpires DateTime?

    playerId Int?

    @@unique([email])
    @@map("user")

model Session {
    id        String   @id
    expiresAt DateTime
    token     String
    createdAt DateTime
    updatedAt DateTime
    ipAddress String?  @db.Text
    userAgent String?  @db.Text
    userId    String

    @@unique([token])
    @@index([userId])
    @@map("session")
}

model Account {

    accountId             String    @db.Text
    providerId            String    @db.Text
    userId                String
    user                  User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
    accessToken           String?   @db.Text
    refreshToken          String?   @db.Text
    idToken               String?   @db.Text
    accessTokenExpiresAt  DateTime?
    refreshTokenExpiresAt DateTime?
    scope                 String?   @db.Text
    password              String?   @db.Text
    createdAt             DateTime
    updatedAt             DateTime

    @@index([userId])
    @@map("account")
}

model Verification {

    identifier String    @db.Text
    value      String    @db.Text
    expiresAt  DateTime

-- Add the new status column as nullable so it can be backfilled before the
-- NOT NULL constraint is enforced.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` ADD COLUMN `status` ENUM('NoGame', 'Scheduled', 'AWin', 'Draw', 'BWin') NULL;

-- Backfill GameDay.status from the columns it replaces:
-- - `game` = FALSE always meant "not an actual match" (covers both a
--   not-yet-scheduled slot and a cancelled one, distinguished only by
--   `mailSent`) -> NoGame.
-- - `game` = TRUE with a unanimous team result recorded in Outcome.points
--   -> AWin / Draw / BWin.
-- - `game` = TRUE with no result, or a non-unanimous ("dirty") one, yet
--   -> Scheduled.
-- Team points are expected to be unanimous within a team whenever a result
-- is decided (the invariant `gameResult.ts::pickTeamPoints` already relied
-- on), but this is verified rather than assumed: COUNT(DISTINCT points) per
-- team must be exactly 1 before that team's points are trusted at all, so a
-- team with mixed/dirty historical data (e.g. 3 and 1) falls back to
-- Scheduled instead of being misclassified via MAX. Verified against the
-- production data snapshot (db-snapshot/GameDay.json + Outcome.json) that no
-- such inconsistency actually exists across any of the 1,326 historical game
-- days, so this backfill produces identical output to the simpler MAX-only
-- version it replaces — this is defence in depth, not a behaviour change.
UPDATE `GameDay` gd
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        `gameDayId`,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aDistinctPoints`,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bDistinctPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'A' THEN `points` END) AS `aPoints`,
        MAX(CASE WHEN `team` = 'B' THEN `points` END) AS `bPoints`
    FROM `Outcome`
    GROUP BY `gameDayId`
) o ON o.`gameDayId` = gd.`id`
SET gd.`status` = CASE
    WHEN gd.`game` = FALSE THEN 'NoGame'
    WHEN o.`aDistinctPoints` <> 1 OR o.`bDistinctPoints` <> 1 THEN 'Scheduled'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 3 AND o.`bPoints` = 0 THEN 'AWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 0 AND o.`bPoints` = 3 THEN 'BWin'
    WHEN o.`aPoints` = 1 AND o.`bPoints` = 1 THEN 'Draw'
    ELSE 'Scheduled'
END;

-- Enforce NOT NULL now that every row has a value, matching the default new
-- game days will get.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` MODIFY COLUMN `status` ENUM('NoGame', 'Scheduled', 'AWin', 'Draw', 'BWin') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Scheduled';

-- Drop the columns status/derived-points now supersede.
ALTER TABLE `GameDay` DROP COLUMN `game`;

ALTER TABLE `Outcome` DROP COLUMN `points`;

-- `score` prefix, pairing with the existing `rank*` prefix (scorePoints goes
-- with rankPoints, etc.) so the bare `points` name is free for the
-- single-game value below.
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord`
    CHANGE COLUMN `averages` `scoreAverages` DOUBLE NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `pub` `scorePub` INTEGER NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `stalwart` `scoreStalwart` INTEGER NULL,
    CHANGE COLUMN `speedy` `scoreSpeedy` INTEGER NULL AFTER `scoreStalwart`;
-- `points` itself is renamed to `scorePoints` via CHANGE COLUMN too, then
-- immediately repurposed below to hold the single-game value instead of the
-- cumulative total (its old meaning now lives in `scorePoints`).
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` CHANGE COLUMN `points` `scorePoints` INTEGER NULL;
ALTER TABLE `PlayerRecord` ADD COLUMN `points` INTEGER NULL;

-- Backfill PlayerRecord.points (the points earned in this specific game,
-- as opposed to the season-cumulative scorePoints) from the same rule as
-- getPlayerPoints (src/lib/gameResult.ts): a team assigned on a decided
-- game day.
UPDATE `PlayerRecord` pr
JOIN `GameDay` gd ON gd.`id` = pr.`gameDayId`
LEFT JOIN `Outcome` o ON o.`gameDayId` = pr.`gameDayId` AND o.`playerId` = pr.`playerId`
SET pr.`points` = CASE
    WHEN o.`team` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'AWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'B' THEN 3
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'BWin' AND o.`team` = 'A' THEN 0
    WHEN gd.`status` = 'Draw' THEN 1
    ELSE NULL
END;
